chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever revives dead land, it is for him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on owning land that has been revived or cultivated?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) traces the principle of 'ihya al-mawat' back to the Prophet Muhammad (PBUAH), establishing it as a Sunnah-based legal maxim. It underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that ownership is acquired through labor and improvement of barren land, a concept deeply rooted in early Islamic economic practices and later elaborated by scholars like al-Shaykh al-Mufid and al-Murtada.
